transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Li (Redwood SE), Priya N. (Redwood CSM), Jamal Ortiz (Aurora CISO), Maya Chen (Aurora SecOps), Liam Rogers (Aurora Platform), Anika Bose (Compliance)

Summary: Quick walkthrough of recent pen test deliverables, discussion of remediation priorities, alignment on patching cadence and SDLC hardening, and confirmation of KMS/customer-managed key options and audit logging/retention. Agreed follow-ups and owners at the end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samira from Redwood, um, joining me is Ethan and Priya. How's everyone doing at Aurora?
[00:12] Jamal: Good, thanks. Busy week after the test but ready to go through the results.
[00:18] Ethan: Cool, so quick agenda — we'll run through high-level findings from the pen test, talk remediation cadence, then SDLC controls we recommend, and lastly KMS/encryption questions.
[00:32] Maya: Sounds good, and we have Anika here for compliance notes.
[00:38] Samira: Great. Quick note — we'll reference the redwood link below, we also have the redacted PDF that we'll share after the call.
[00:46] Liam: Perfect.
[01:05] Ethan: Ok, top-level from the pen test: seven medium-to-high findings. Number one was XSS in the patient portal's message view — reflected as a stored XSS; number two SSRF outbound to internal metadata endpoints; number three some outdated third-party libs flagged by SCA; number four misconfigured S3 ACLs, five weak session timeout config, six potential RCE in a rarely used worker, and seven info disclosure in debug endpoints. My apologies if I mis-state the exact vuln names, the full report has verbatim output.
[01:40] Jamal: The SSRF flagged us — that one concerns me for data egress to the metadata service where our instance creds live.
[01:47] Ethan: Right, that's the main critical-ish callout. For SSRF the typical mitigation is egress filtering and metadata service IMDSv2 enforcement, and code-level input validation; plus network egress rules from the service subnet.
[02:12] Maya: We're on IMDSv1 kind of by default on some legacy images, so that's on us. We have an internal ticket to flip to IMDSv2 but it's not across all fleets.
[02:26] Samira: Ok noted — that's a low-effort high-impact fix. We'll mark as priority.
[02:35] [02:36] Speaker 5: (inaudible)
[03:01] Ethan: On the third-party libs — SCA flagged about 12 libs, a couple are transitive and used by that worker process. Recommended action is SCA+pinning plus a weekly BOM scan in CI.
[03:20] Jamal: We're closing dependency issues on a sprint by sprint basis but cadence is more like monthly triage. Might need to tighten.
[03:28] Ethan: For secure SDLC we recommend shifting critical security upgrades to a 2-week hotfix lane for high severity CVEs, 30-day for medium, and 90-day for low. That dovetails with patching cadence discussion later.
[03:48] Maya: Do you have suggested SLAs for patching windows?
[03:52] Ethan: We usually recommend 48-72 hours for critical public exploits, 14-30 days for high, 30-60 for medium depending on exposure. For healthcare workloads, aim for a more aggressive drop-down.
[04:10] Anika: From a compliance perspective, we need documented evidence of patch timelines for SOC2.
[04:16] Samira: We'll include templates you can use for audit logs and patch evidence.
[04:25] [04:40] Ethan: On encryption/KMS — Aurora asked about customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM-backed KMS. Redwood supports CMK for private deployments; in hosted we offer customer-managed KMS via integration with major cloud KMS providers and optional HSM through partner channels. Keep in mind there is an operational tradeoff: BYOK adds key rotation and backup responsibilities.
[05:03] Liam: For PHI we want customer-controlled key lifecycle. Can Redwood support Bring-Your-Own-KEY and log KMS operations to our SIEM?
[05:14] Ethan: Yes — you can onboard a KMS key and we can emit KMS operation audit events to your log forwarder (we've done Splunk, Sumo, Datadog). There is a small latency bump on cold starts for key unwrap, but negligible for steady-state.
[05:32] Maya: What's the retention window for KMS audit logs and general Redwood audit logs?
[05:37] Samira: Default retention is 90 days in hosted; for enterprise customers we can extend to 12 months or mirror to your long-term storage depending on plan. That's covered in the enterprise compliance addendum.
[05:54] Jamal: Good — we need 12 months for SOC2 evidence.
[06:01] Samira: Noted.
[06:15] [06:30] Ethan: Back to the pen test — about the worker RCE: the exploit chain required a rarely used debug endpoint plus an outdated native lib. Recommended: remove or auth-protect debug endpoints, upgrade the native lib, and add SAST around native code.
[06:52] Liam: That debug endpoint was kept for dev ops access, we can gate it behind a VPN or require mTLS.
[07:01] Ethan: mTLS is good. Also add RBAC and SSO controls — for Redwood we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and can map groups to RBAC roles for per-token scoping.
[07:20] Maya: Do you have a doc for RBAC role mapping and least-privilege guidance?
[07:25] Samira: Yes, we'll share the RBAC guide. Link: https://redwood.example.com/security/rbac-guide (redacted link).
[07:33] [07:45] Jamal: On SAML/SCIM — we have Okta and Azure AD; how mature is the SCIM provisioning?
[07:51] Ethan: SCIM is supported for user provisioning and group sync. For SAML we do SP-initiated SSO and SCIM for provisioning; for private deployments we can support SCIM over your private endpoint.
[08:10] Anika: Audit logs — what fields are included? We need event user, action, resource, timestamp, source IP, and KMS key id for any crypto ops.
[08:22] Ethan: Our audit schema covers user, service token, resource path, verb, timestamp, request ID, source IP, and for KMS events we include keyId and operation. We'll share the schema.
[08:37] Maya: Can you redact PII in logs by default?
[08:40] Samira: We can mask or not log payloads; typically we log metadata only, not full request bodies. For PHI you might choose to disable request body logging entirely.
[08:53] [09:05] Ethan: About data residency — Aurora asked about EU-only regions for backups and logs; hosted Redwood can pin regions and we can restrict storage to a region. For private deployments you control data plane entirely.
[09:23] Jamal: We'll likely go with a hybrid — hosted control plane but private data plane in our VPC.
[09:30] Samira: That's a common pattern; we support it. We'll provide the architecture diagram and the VPC peering docs.
[09:41] [10:00] Ethan: Quick note on KV cache references in the report — some names in the transcript might show "K V cache" or mis-typed. The important part is prefix cache leakage risk test failed for a narrow set of prefixes — mitigation is cache key isolation per-tenant and TTLs.
[10:20] Liam: Ok we'll need implementation guidance for tenant isolation in the cache layer.
[10:26] Ethan: We'll add code snippets.
[10:33] [11:00] Maya: Patch cadence — we operate on a quarterly full patch for infra but security-critical hotfixes are ad-hoc. We need a formal cadence that satisfies SOC2.
[11:12] Samira: Recommend: establish a security-response policy that defines windows for critical/high/medium/low, include evidence capture in the ticketing system, and an executive dashboard. Redwood's console has token-level change logs and can surface patch states for endpoints in the dedicated/private fleet.
[11:35] Jamal: Is there automation for patch deployment and can we exclude canary hosts?
[11:41] Ethan: Yes — you can define canary groups, rollout % and automated rollback on health checks. We'll show the Dedicated autoscale/rollout UI in the follow-up demo.
[11:56] [12:20] Priya: We'll attach a sample remediation matrix and patch policy template in the follow-up email.
[12:28] Anika: About vulnerability triage — do you recommend a single queue or per-team? Our org needs traceability for auditors.
[12:36] Ethan: Per-team triage with a centralized tracker is best; the tracker should link to CVE, risk rating, exploitability, and remediation ticket. Include timestamps for discovery, mitigation, and verification.
[12:55] [13:15] Jamal: Any thoughts on running an internal red team vs third party? We used a third party this time but want to build internal capabilities.
[13:22] Samira: Third-party is great for compliance; internal red team is good for continuous testing. You can do both: scheduled 3rd-party pen test annually and internal rotating purple team exercises quarterly.
[13:38] Ethan: We'll also recommend integrating canary tokens and deception tech in sensitive flows.
[13:50] [14:05] Liam: For remediation testing — how do we validate that fixes didn't regress latency or CPU on the inference path?
[14:12] Ethan: Redwood has canary traffic tooling and per-route latency dashboards, plus token-level cost traces. Run regression tests in staging with representative payloads and use the trace hooks.
[14:28] Maya: Can we run a benchmark of the patched worker in a dedicated cluster?
[14:34] Ethan: Yes we can schedule a dedicated bench with our performance team; we'll need the binary/version and test vectors.
[14:45] [15:00] Samira: Quick admin — we'll send the redacted pen test report to Anika and Jamal, include remediation matrix, RBAC guide, KMS integration doc, and SOC2 evidence pack.
[15:13] Anika: Please remove any PII from the redacted report.
[15:17] Samira: Yes, we'll scrub PII.
[15:30] [16:00] Ethan: One last technical nit — S3 ACL misconfig: ensure buckets default to private and use bucket policies for cross-account access; prefer presigned URLs for short-lived access.
[16:18] Jamal: We'll remediate that in our infra sprint next week.
[16:25] [17:00] Maya: For evidence collection — is there a sample SOC2 artifact map?
[17:06] Priya: Yes, we'll attach a SOC2 artifact checklist with expected docs and examples.
[17:18] Samira: All right, recap of next steps — Ethan to produce remediation matrix, Samira to share docs, Liam to give host list and patch baseline, schedule KMS deep-dive.
[17:36] [18:00] Jamal: Thanks everyone, super helpful.
[18:05] Samira: Thanks, we'll follow up with links.
[18:10] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: intermittent mis-labeling of product names (eg. K-V cache, Redwood Priva), some speaker labels collapsed to generic 'Speaker 5' during crosstalk.
